title: The Fer expansion of a driven spin under $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ operations cannot terminate beyond first order
authors: Lorenzo Bagnasacco, Daniel Burgarth, Vittorio Giovannetti, Kazuya Yuasa
abstract: The Fer expansion writes the propagator of a driven quantum system as an ordered product of exponentials, each generated by the time integral of an effective Hamiltonian that governs the evolution left over by the previous factors. It can be stopped after finitely many factors whenever this leftover evolution is known in closed form, for instance when the effective Hamiltonian commutes with itself at all times, or precesses about a fixed axis with constant angular velocity. For $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, in any representation, from a qubit to a spin of any size, we resum the Fer recursion into a closed map on curves in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We prove that, for a real-analytic drive, in both cases the expansion stops beyond the first factor only trivially, when the first exponential is already exact.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the mathematical structure of the Fer expansion for driven quantum spins under $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ symmetry. It proves that the expansion, which decomposes the time evolution into a product of exponentials, can only terminate after a finite number of steps if the initial driving Hamiltonian is already highly constrained. This places strong mathematical restrictions on the dynamics that can be described by a simple, finite product form.
main_problem: The paper investigates the termination condition of the Fer expansion, a method for writing the propagator of a driven quantum system as an ordered product of exponentials.
main_result: For $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ systems driven by a real-analytic Hamiltonian, the Fer expansion cannot terminate after a finite number of factors unless the original drive already belongs to a specific, highly constrained family (Family A).
method: The analysis uses the structure of the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Lie algebra, deriving closed-form maps for the recursive coefficients of the expansion and proving termination conditions via algebraic constraints.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum spin governed by $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ operations, whose time evolution is described by a time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t)$. The analysis focuses on the mathematical structure of the resulting time-ordered exponential (the Fer expansion).
key_observables: The coefficients $h_j(t)$ defining the effective Hamiltonians at each order $j$, and the condition for the recursion to map into the set $A$.
important_parameters: The drive function $h_1(t)$ must be real-analytic; the algebra is $\mathfrak{su}(2)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to real-analytic drives, and the mathematical machinery relies on the validity of series expansions and the structure of the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ algebra.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates one step of the Fer map on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, showing the projection and transformation of the drive vector into components for the next effective Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general theory of the Fer expansion, derives the specific closed-form map for $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ using techniques like conjugation by exponentials, and culminates in proving that finite termination requires the initial drive to be trivial (i.e., in Family A).
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural insights into the non-commutativity of time-ordered exponentials for spin systems, which is crucial for understanding quantum dynamics in open or time-varying fields.
